### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via diffItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.diffItem, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/diff), meta.diffItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/diff, selected by route anchor /:type/:name/diff))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b60eb78d35044949839e383823b228bcaf67dec4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19af244d1fe0378e9a2917efe2c14705ba70cc78` — the merge of head `d8f08c015ecf392db9acee90eb28643ac95c19c1` into base `b60eb78d35044949839e383823b228bcaf67dec4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19af244d1fe0378e9a2917efe2c14705ba70cc78 && git checkout 19af244d1fe0378e9a2917efe2c14705ba70cc78
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b60eb78d35044949839e383823b228bcaf67dec4 d8f08c015ecf392db9acee90eb28643ac95c19c1 && git checkout -B drift-repro b60eb78d35044949839e383823b228bcaf67dec4 && git merge --no-ff d8f08c015ecf392db9acee90eb28643ac95c19c1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b60eb78d35044949839e383823b228bcaf67dec4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b60eb78d35044949839e383823b228bcaf67dec4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

`domain:spec` seat 4 (#18917) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · claim `6163983419` on #23183 · reviewed head `d8f08c015ecf392db9acee90eb28643ac95c19c1` · 2026-10-14T11:26Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 23468`), 10 files, +699 / −2. It lands after the landing clauses in item 6.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #23183`, `Clause-②: yes` at line start. The changeset is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: spec and metadata-protocol `minor`, rest `patch`. No other closing keyword sits beside a card number.
2. **Premises against the dispatch's ruling (seat decision with a premise, adopting triage `6140092978`).**
   - The arm: `GET /meta/app/:key` accepts a package id for `type: 'app'` only, and answers the by-name verdict. A withheld app answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. An unknown package, a package with no app, an unpublished app and a multi-app package answer the 404 absence answer, byte-identical to an unknown name. A holder is served the app under its own `name`. There is no separate endpoint, and no other type gains the arm.
   - The premise held on both halves, measured: the grammars are disjoint (`AppSchema.name` is snake_case, `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` needs a dot, and every mint path holds it). Disclosure is no wider: an unpublished app's package answers like an unknown one, and the 403 echoes the caller's key, never the app name.
   - Spec first: `GetMetaItemRequestSchema.name` declares the arm in its describe, and `isAppPackageIdKey(type, name)` is its one spelling.
   - A `packageId` naming a different package answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, an existing ledger code.
3. **Gates and evidence.** Reviewed with CI converging on this head: 22 success, 5 skipped, 11 in progress, 0 failures. The producer pin covers 8 cases. The two-host wire pin (`meta-app-package-id-key.test.ts`) covers 12 rows: 403, 404 and served on both hosts, by-name unchanged, a dotted key on a non-app type unchanged, and `/history` and `/diff` staying by name. Both ablations went red on exactly their predicted rows (A 5/3, B 2/10).
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - The runtime half landed in the producer (`metadata-protocol` `getMetaItem`, `resolveAppPackageIdKey`), not in `rest-server.ts`. The card clause allows that, and the dev flagged it rather than choosing it silently: both hosts hand the protocol the raw key and judge through the same answer chain, so one resolution reaches both.
   - `rest-server.ts` changes only `fetchCurrentMetaDocument`, which keeps `/history`, `/audit` and `/diff` by name. Without it, a holder's `/diff` turns 404 into an empty 200.
   - One row was added to `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` through the gate's `--write`.
   - Four local families are NOT MEASURED (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`). CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` on this head are the reading.
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - `check:type-check-debt`'s re-measure runs a full workspace build outside the shared verify lock, and measurably rewrote `dist/` under a locked test run (a false red): filed as #23470.
   - The two stale `rest-server.ts` comments, routed to "the next dispatch that touches the file" since 2026-09-29: dropped. They are internal comments, and one names two of a shape's three tombstones; the dev re-measured them as at most partially stale. That is not a defect class, and riding the next PR is no longer a carrier.
   - Acceptance notes, `carrier:` none: a pre-grammar residue app row whose name has a dot would read as a package id; a disabled package's app answers 404 by package id. Both are read-only inferences, no producer can mint the first, and the second was not measured on the wire.
   - Consumer pointer for objectstack-ai/objectui#12285: posted on that card when this PR lands.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) A `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` `## Contract review` PASS on the landing head: published schema face (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) plus the `Clause-②: yes` declaration.
   - (b) Every check green on the landing head.
   - (c) `mergeable_state` clean at enqueue. PR #23464 also edits `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, in `deleteMetaItem`'s region; whichever lands second resolves, per §10.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d8f08c015ecf392db9acee90eb28643ac95c19c1`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23183 (body and all six comments, triage's accept-set choice `6140092978`, regrades `6163056202` and `6163499879`, the claim `6163983419`, the `os-dev-report` `6167194448`, the accept `6167274878`), PR #23468 (body, 10-file list, net diff against `main` at the head, merge-base `7cfc3400c1`: 699 added, 2 deleted, 701 changed lines, head repo equals base repo, no governed path), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only throughout: the head was fetched into a ref of its own and read with `git show`; nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept set the card and triage chose is one read: `GET /meta/app/KEY` accepts a package id as its key, for `type: app` only, answering the by-name verdict (403 withheld, 404 absent, 200 held), no separate verdict endpoint, no other type. Every change the diff implies, judged against that:

1. **Spec, `GetMetaItemRequestSchema.name` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) — right.** The describe declares the arm exactly as chosen: `app` only, a key in the package-id grammar names the package, the package's one app answered under its own `name`, the per-caller gate's 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, absence for a package with no app or more than one, 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` for a `packageId` naming a different package, every other type and key by name. It is the protocol METHOD contract (the `GET /:type/:name` route entry in `plugin-rest-api.zod.ts`, handler `getMetaItem`, declares no request body schema by design), so the spec states the arm before the runtime serves it, as the card asks. The disjoint-grammar premise holds at the head: `AppSchema.name` is `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` (lowercase snake_case, no dot) and `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` requires at least one dot. The describe, the thrown refusal and the operator warning carry no tracker number.

2. **New export `isAppPackageIdKey(type, name)` — right.** One predicate, `type === 'app'` and `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN.test(name)`, the single spelling both consumers ask (the producer and the REST guard); a contract predicate in the vein of `isSubscribableChannel`, not business logic. It takes the canonical singular type and both callers fold first (`canonicalizeMetaRequestType` in the protocol, `metaTypeSingular` in REST; both map `apps` to `app`). `api-surface/api.json`, `export-origins/api.json` and `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` are regenerated (0 breaking, 1 added); the JSON-schema and authorable-surface shards key the schema without its describe text, so no other artifact was owed (the old describe text has zero occurrences at the head).

3. **Producer-side resolution, `resolveAppPackageIdKey` at the top of `getMetaItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) — right, and right to land there rather than in `rest-server.ts`.** Both transports hand the protocol the raw key and judge the envelope through the same `createMetaItemAnswer` chain, whose own docblock says an item step is added there and never in a transport: RestServer's plain read (its cached arm is excluded for `app` by the `!isAppType` condition, so an app read always takes the uncached arm and the served envelope is the protocol's, under the app's own name), the runtime dispatcher's item read and its `readPendingDraft`. Leak check: `getMetaItemCached` delegates to `getMetaItem` and keeps no server-side store keyed by name (ETag over content and locale only); `saveMetaItem`'s internal `getMetaItem` is guarded `singularType === 'object'`, so the arm cannot reach the save path; `publish`, `rollback`, `delete`, `/published` and `/layers` read other protocol methods and gain no arm (consistent with "the existing app item read"); no other non-test consumer in the repo passes `type: 'app'`. Per case:
   - **One app:** the request becomes that app's by-name read scoped prefer-local to the package (`packageId` set), so the stored row, the lock and the version token are the app's own; the envelope names the app, the address a save uses. Right.
   - **Zero apps, unknown package:** the request is returned untouched and the by-name read of a dotted key answers absence, byte-identical to an unknown app name (pinned on both hosts). Right.
   - **Multi-app:** absence, plus one `console.warn` per package and app set, naming the apps and the remedy. Right: a distinct answer would disclose an app being built in the package before publish (ADR-0045 §3); at-most-one is ADR-0019 D3, enforced only by `defineStack` for `manifest.type === 'app'`; a functional degradation told once at `warn` is the level the repo's rule prescribes. Each app stays readable by its own name.
   - **Unpublished:** the package-scoped list includes the `_unpublished` app, so the key resolves and the per-caller gate (`filterAppForUserWithReason`, ADR-0045 §3 judged first) answers absence to a non-builder and the app to a builder, exactly as by name; the wire test pins unpublished-package bytes equal to unknown-package bytes for a member. Right.
   - **Drafts:** `previewDrafts: true` is passed to the list exactly when the read reads drafts (`state: 'draft'` or `previewDrafts`), and `readFlattenedMetaItems` merges draft rows under that flag, so a draft-only app resolves on the draft read and not on the plain one. Right.
   - **Conflicting `packageId`:** 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` thrown before any read (a pure request-shape refusal, no existence oracle); the same package is the same read; `metaItemPackageBinding` folds `?package=all` and the empty value to no package, so neither conflicts. The code and status match the spelling refusal at the same request boundary. Right.
   - **Store outage:** no `catch`; a failed list read propagates, so an outage is never answered as "no such package". Right.
   - **Disabled package:** `registry.listItems` hides a disabled package's items while `registry.getItem` does not, so by package id such an app answers 404 where by name it is still served. The key is defined against the package-scoped list (the read behind `GET /meta/app?package=`), with which it agrees; the asymmetry is the by-name read's and predates this PR. Noted, not a defect of this diff (③).

4. **Disclosure — a non-holder learns nothing the by-name read would not tell them. Right.** The 403 message is built from the gate's `name` argument, which is the URL key on both hosts (`req.params.name` on REST, the dispatched `name` on the catch-all), so the package-to-app-name mapping is never echoed; the 200 is served only to a holder; unpublished, service-gated, no-app, multi-app and unknown all collapse to one absence answer; the 400 is pre-read. What is newly learnable is only that a package ships a withheld app, which is the same oracle the by-name 403 already is (a probe implies the key), as triage's disclosure reading states. Enumeration is no wider.

5. **The `/history` `/audit` `/diff` guard in `rest-server.ts` (`fetchCurrentMetaDocument` returns no document for a package-id key) — right.** Those doors read their own data under the literal `:name` while judging "the item the plain read would judge" through `getMetaItem`; without the guard they would judge the resolved app yet serve the key's empty events, turning a non-holder's `/history` from 200 to 403 and a holder's `/diff` from the absence answer to a 200 empty diff (the two reds the dev's ablation B reproduced). The guard keeps those doors byte-identical to before the arm (`/diff` falls to `sendMetaItemAbsent` because `gatesOnItsOwnKey('app')` is false). `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` has exactly those two consumers (`eventDoorRefusal` and the `/diff` handler), it folds the type through `metaTypeSingular` before asking the predicate, and `meta-item-read-gate.ts` is untouched. Giving those doors the arm instead would be a second read beyond "one read, not two". The dispatcher serves none of these doors.

6. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` row (`protocol.app-package-id-key.test.ts`, `findOne`, pinned 1) — right.** The harness's `findOne` double routes through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which is the gate's `findOne` slice; the ledger is the grow-only RETAINED ledger that `--write` regenerates (its own `$comment`), and the row sits in the file's sorted order. A coverage gain, not debt.

7. **Tests — right for the accept set.** The producer test pins one app (singular and plural spelling), the unchanged by-name read, no app and unknown package, multi-app with one report, the `packageId` conflict (code and status), a dotted key on `view` where a package of that id ships an app, and drafts. The wire test drives RestServer and the hono catch-all over a real sqlite store each and pins all five triage pins on both hosts, the absence bytes, unpublished equals unknown, and the three REST-only doors by name. Neither test reads outside its package by path (module imports only); the runtime rig is a sibling's.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23183-app-item-read-by-package-id.md` declares `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`. That matches what the diff publishes: spec adds one export and widens a describe (api-surface 0 breaking, 1 added), so `minor`; metadata-protocol gives `getMetaItem` a new accept set, so `minor`; rest publishes only the guard that holds three doors at their pre-arm answers, its wire gaining the arm through the protocol it is handed, so `patch` (a `minor` would also have been defensible; `patch` is not wrong). `@objectstack/runtime` changes a test file only and owes no changeset. All three are published packages.
- `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset body agree; `yes` takes at least `minor`, which spec carries, and the `(widening)` arm is the non-breaking one, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. `Check Changeset` is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (`os-dev-report` `6167194448`, `deviations`), each answered:
1. **File surface** (the producer in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, a wire test in `@objectstack/runtime`, the import and export beside the schema, `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` rather than the plain read handler) — accepted. The card leaves the carrier to the owning seat and asks spec-first; the claim said to stop on a breach and explain it in the report, which the report does; the producer is where both hosts' item reads converge, so the landing is the right one (① item 3). The `protocol.zod.ts` hunks sit at the import block and at the schema itself, none at the describe regions the claim names for #23428.
2. **Ledger row** against the preference for reusing a double — accepted: no existing metadata-protocol double models a package-scoped app registry, and the gate prescribes `--write` (① item 6).
3. **Overlapping local runs** — process only; the final readings were re-run alone, and the gate verdicts here are CI's.
4. **Declared narrowing** (full spec and runtime suites left to CI) — closed by `Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)` and the `Test Core` summary, all `success`.
5. **Attribution** — the six branch commits carry the model-free session trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes; no model identifier in any commit, the PR body, the changeset, the docs or the code.

`open_questions`: empty; nothing to answer.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each carried or answered:
- `check:type-check-debt` `refreshBuiltClosure` rebuilding dists beside the verify lock — filed by the seat as #23470 (accept `6167274878`).
- Two stale `rest-server.ts` comments (`api.documentation` tombstones, `parseDeclaredApiConfig`) — outside the touched region; carrier the next spec or cli dispatch on that file; noted.
- A pre-grammar residue `app` row with a dotted name would now be read as a package id — no producer can mint one (the save door's name agreement plus `AppSchema`; `defineStack`'s `AppSchema`), and the row stays listable and deletable; noted, not filed.
- A disabled package's app answers 404 by package id while the by-name read serves it — a read-only inference, agreeing with the package-scoped list the key is defined against; the asymmetry is the by-name read's and predates this PR. Does not hold this PR; the seat may file it as its own card once measured on the wire.
- Consumer note for objectstack-ai/objectui#12285 — matches the read as landed: `client.meta.getItem('app', packageId)` encodes the name and dotted names already travel that door; the existing `probeMetaItemAccess` mapping (403 denied, absence not_found, 200 granted) reads it unchanged.

Gate verdicts, read last (2026-10-14T11:57Z, after the last run completed at 11:52:05Z): 41 check-runs on the head, 36 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance: the full-battery and opt-in set that does not run on a PR), 0 `failure`, 0 `in_progress`. The five required contexts are all `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard.
